paragraphs: Arc 1, paragraph beginning Inês opens the Account Tokens page
Arc 9, paragraph beginning pagecraft-app expires on 3 May
Frame: actor table row for the Pagecraft app, Credential column
rulings.rule: A stated cause that never happens; content that does not bear out the step's name.
rulings.reason: The story makes Vercel project environment changes and a redeployment causal prerequisites for the application's first use and token rotation, but the corresponding life performs token creation and a wait alone. These are Vercel acts, not merely an external registrar premise.
rulings.requiredChange: Narrow the story to the credential handoff actually represented: in act 1 replace the claim of saving VERCEL_TOKEN in project settings with Inês copying the newly shown token for the application calls; in act 9 replace the environment-setting/redeployment/live-deployment claims with Inês copying the replacement token, switching the subsequent represented application calls to it, then deleting the old token. Describe the stale-credential refusal as a call with the revoked token, without asserting a particular deployment or pending-domain cron. Align the frame credential row (which presently says in the project's env as VERCEL_TOKEN) with that narrower captured-credential handoff. No new Vercel deployment implementation is required.

paragraphs: Arc 6, paragraph beginning Carla enters carlayoga.pt
Arc 10, paragraph beginning Alice closes her ordering page
Arc 11, paragraph beginning Dmitri closes his Pagecraft account
rulings.rule: A read-back with no need, unless someone who does not hold it reads it.
rulings.reason: The life appends project-domain GETs immediately after each successful removal, but these paragraphs provide no separate reader or business reason for those checks.
rulings.requiredChange: State that the respective customer subsequently opens or refreshes their Pagecraft domain settings, whose request handler reads current Vercel association state without the deletion response. Make the corresponding life GET name identify that customer action. Alternatively remove those GETs entirely and rely on the already-motivated nightly reconciliation; the outline must not promise a separate verification read without its cause.

doubts.reason: Alice's one-minute retry has an explicit user uncertainty cause and a separate wait, so it is not ruled a same-sitting repeat; the separation is thin.
Writing a life asks for prose with no calls, while this outline embeds operation paths. This is a presentation/procedure concern rather than a plausibility rejection listed in What a judge rejects.
